findings.issue_text: Count-then-insert in CreateOrUpdateDevice is not atomic (TOCTOU race): concurrent requests can all observe count == limit-1 and insert, exceeding the configured device limit; ErrDeviceLimitReached from updateDevice also conflates 'limit reached' with 'device row doesn't exist / outside window', making the sentinel's meaning fuzzy for callers

Authenticate hard-fails anonymous auth by returning ErrDeviceLimitReached as a raw untyped sentinel error instead of wrapping it in an authn-framework error (e.g., mapping to errUnauthenticated), so denied devices may surface as 500 Internal Server Error rather than a clean 401/denial

Existing devices inactive for >30 days (row present but outside the BETWEEN window, not yet cleaned up) get ErrDeviceLimitReached and are permanently denied — they can neither be updated nor re-created until cleanup frees a slot, causing hard lockout with no recovery path

MySQL no-op update can spuriously deny an existing active device: rowsAffected == 0 is treated exclusively as 'limit reached / device unknown', but on MySQL ROWS_AFFECTED counts changed rows (no CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS) at second-precision timestamps, so an identical update within the same second yields 0 affected rows and ErrDeviceLimitReached; SQLite-based tests won't catch this

The 1-minute upper bound in updateDevice's updated_at BETWEEN window breaks under clock skew: comparing this instance's clock against updated_at written by another instance's clock means >1 minute skew (or NTP step-back) puts an active device outside the window, causing ErrDeviceLimitReached and denial of active devices

Tagging moved onto the synchronous request path with panic containment removed: goroutine, context.WithTimeout, and recover() were removed, so every anonymous request performs synchronous DB work (CountDevices plus a write) on the auth critical path, and panics in TagDevice propagate into the authn flow instead of being logged and contained

Anonymous access can be trivially denied (DoS) once the device limit is reached, by a single unauthenticated client varying device identity (IP/User-Agent) to exhaust the limit and lock out all anonymous users (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-52, anonstore/database.go:103-110)

Returning devices inactive for more than 30 days but not yet garbage-collected (deletion window ~61 days) match 0 rows in the updateDevice 'updated_at BETWEEN' window and get ErrDeviceLimitReached, even though admitting them cannot exceed the limit — a correctness bug with user-facing availability impact (anonstore/database.go:73-92)
Count-then-insert in CreateOrUpdateDevice is not atomic, so concurrent first-time device requests can pass the check and exceed deviceLimit (TOCTOU) (anonstore/database.go:103-110)

ErrDeviceLimitReached propagates out of Authenticate into the authn pipeline, externally surfacing raw internal error text and a likely non-graceful status (500-style) to unauthenticated users instead of a proper redirect/anonymous-denied page (client.go:44-52)

AnonymousDeviceLimit is exposed to all clients via the unauthenticated /frontend/settings payload, disclosing the configured anonymous capacity with no apparent consumer need (pkg/api/frontendsettings.go:198, pkg/api/dtos/frontend_settings.go:195)

Synchronous COUNT(*) added to authentication hot path: client.go removed fire-and-forget goroutine so TagDevice is now fully synchronous inside Authenticate, and every CreateOrUpdateDevice call with deviceLimit > 0 runs CountDevices (a COUNT(*) query) before any insert/update, causing a potential table scan on anon_device per invocation and a latency/DB-load amplifier under high device churn

Count-then-insert TOCTOU race: the count check and insert in CreateOrUpdateDevice are not atomic, so under concurrent requests N simultaneous new devices can all observe count < limit and all insert, overshooting the device limit; the ErrDeviceLimitReached compensation in updateDevice only kicks in for the next request

Once the device limit is reached, every returning (cached-out) device still pays the expensive COUNT query before its cheap UPDATE, doubling work on the steady-state path; a conditional UPDATE first with COUNT only when rowsAffected == 0 would be cheaper

ListDevices API returns unbounded result set with no pagination or LIMIT, materializing all devices in the 30-day window into a single JSON response, which can spike memory and response time on the Grafana server

ErrDeviceLimitReached propagates out of Authenticate as an authentication failure, so once the device limit is hit new anonymous users get hard auth errors; combined with the TOCTOU race an attacker can race-fill the limit and lock out all subsequent new anonymous visitors (denial-of-service-by-design)

P1: In updateDevice (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:73-90), on MySQL an UPDATE that matches a row but sets identical values reports 0 rows affected, so with second-granularity timestamps, parallel requests in the same second cause RowsAffected()==0 and spurious ErrDeviceLimitReached for already-known devices; should use RowsAffected()==0 && RowsMatched()==0 or check existence separately

P1: Undefined HTTP contract when device limit is hit (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-53): Authenticate now returns raw anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached which is not a recognized authn error type, leaving the HTTP response (401 vs 500, redirect vs JSON, message exposure) undefined; needs deliberate error mapping or should proceed unauthenticated instead of failing auth

P2: Synchronous DB write plus CountDevices query added to the anonymous request hot path (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-53): the goroutine + context.WithTimeout + panic recovery was removed, causing latency/DB-load regression on every anonymous request

P2: TagDevice now runs with the request context instead of a detached context (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-53), so client-disconnected/aborted requests silently lose device tagging that was previously guaranteed to complete in the background
P2: A panic in TagDevice is no longer recovered and logged (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-53) and can now propagate into the authn flow and surface as a 500

P2: Response-shape drift (pkg/api/dtos/frontend_settings.go:195, packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200, packages/grafana-runtime/src/config.ts:97): AnonymousDeviceLimit is int64 without omitempty so the server always sends a number, but the TS type declares number | undefined; undefined can never arrive, making '!== undefined' checks dead code, and the 0-vs-undefined semantics are undocumented; pick one sentinel

P3: TOCTOU race in CreateOrUpdateDevice (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:94-102): count-then-act with no transaction, lock, or conditional insert lets concurrent first-arrivals exceed the configured device limit; consider a conditional insert mechanism like the updateDevice guard

P3: Wire constructor signature changes (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:37-46, anonstore/database.go:57-59): ProvideAnonymousDeviceService drops the anonStore parameter and ProvideAnonDBStore gains one, but no wire_gen.go update appears in the diff; a stale wire set would cause a build/initialization failure
P1: Synchronous DB call in anonymous auth hot path with no timeout — removal of detached goroutine with context.WithTimeout means slow/hanging DB blocks every anonymous request (client.go:44-49)
P1: Lost crash isolation — old goroutine had recover(), now a panic in TagDevice propagates into auth path and fails the request instead of just logging a warning (client.go:44-49)

P1: Race condition in CreateOrUpdateDevice — CountDevices and INSERT are non-transactional, concurrent requests can all observe count < limit and insert, unboundedly exceeding the device limit (database.go:106-114)

P2: RowsAffected == 0 conflates 'device missing' with 'no rows changed' in MySQL — DSN without clientFoundRows=true returns rows changed, so an existing device with identical values gets spurious ErrDeviceLimitReached (database.go:72-92)

P2: Clock-skew window in updateDevice — hardcoded +1 minute tolerance in BETWEEN guard means devices with updated_at slightly in the future are locked out until the deletion job removes them, up to 30+ days (database.go:71-83)
P2: ErrDeviceLimitReached sentinel error surfaced through Authenticate with no HTTP status mapping or user-facing message, producing opaque hard failure for anonymous visitors (client.go:46-48)

P3: Additional DB round-trip per anonymous request — CountDevices aggregate plus conditional write on every cache-miss tagging creates hot-path cost and load amplifier during traffic spikes (database.go:106-113)

P3: Frontend config type declares AnonymousDeviceLimit as number | undefined but backend DTO always serializes a number (0 when unset), causing inconsistent behavior for logic branching on === undefined (config.ts:200 / frontend_settings.go:195)

P1: Missing test coverage for updateDevice success path — no test calls updateDevice with an existing device_id within the 30-day window and asserts no error and that client_ip, user_agent, and updated_at are persisted

P1: Significant behavioral change to Authenticate with no corresponding test — TagDevice is now synchronous (blocking auth on DB latency) and ErrDeviceLimitReached now fails authentication entirely, with no test verifying anonymous auth errors on limit hit or succeeds on non-limit TagDevice failure
P2: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks the error and never asserts database state via ListDevices to confirm the rejected device was not inserted and exactly one device row remains
P2: Boundary condition of the device limit (count == limit-1 → create succeeds; count == limit → rejected) is only half-covered (limit=1 only)

P2: No edge-case coverage for expired devices interacting with the limit — a device with updated_at older than 30 days is excluded from the count but also from the updateDevice BETWEEN window, so it can never refresh itself and always receives ErrDeviceLimitReached; behavior of stale/expired devices under a configured limit is unpinned

P2: Config propagation to frontend is untested — AnonymousDeviceLimit int64 serializes as 0 when unset, but the TS type is number | undefined and runtime default is undefined, so consumers may interpret 0 as 'limit of zero devices'; no test asserts the serialized payload for configured and unconfigured cases
P2: No coverage for the TagDevice contract change in impl.go — tagDeviceUI errors were previously swallowed (logged, returned nil) and are now propagated, but no test exercises the failure path

P3: Check-then-act race on the device limit (CountDevices + conditional insert) is untested — concurrent anonymous requests can overshoot the limit, and no concurrency test documents whether slight overshoot is acceptable

P1: Device limit is trivially exhaustible — anonymous device identity is client-supplied, so an attacker can fill the device table with fresh device IDs up to the limit, causing a hard authentication failure (error page, not login redirect) for all new anonymous devices; entries persist 30 days and recovery requires admin intervention; the exact limit is exposed to unauthenticated clients via FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit, and there is no rate limiting on the first-seen/create path (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-48, pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:97-103)

P2: TOCTOU race in CreateOrUpdateDevice — CountDevices then insert is not atomic (no transaction, row lock, or INSERT ... WHERE count < limit guard), so N concurrent requests from new devices can all observe count < limit and all insert, exceeding the limit (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:95-103)

P2: updateDevice conflates rowsAffected == 0 with 'device limit reached' — zero affected rows can have unrelated causes (MySQL changed-rows semantics without CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS when values are identical due to DATETIME second precision, or clock skew in HA deployments where a future updated_at from a node running ahead causes the BETWEEN match to fail), spuriously blocking legitimate known devices with a device-limit error (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:72-93)

P2: Tagging moved onto the synchronous request path with panic recovery removed — previously fire-and-forget goroutine with recover() and detached 2-minute timeout, now any panic in the tagging chain propagates into authentication and fails the request, and every anonymous request's latency now includes the store round-trip so DB slowness stalls all anonymous traffic (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-50)

P3: Device limit silently fails open on any DB error — if CountDevices or the store call returns any error other than ErrDeviceLimitReached, the device is not registered and the error is only warn-logged, so during DB degradation the limit is silently unenforced with no operator signal (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:97-101, pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:50-52)

P3: Test gap — TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only asserts a new device gets ErrDeviceLimitReached; it never verifies that an existing in-window device still succeeds via updateDevice when count >= limit, nor that the device count didn't grow, so regressions in the BETWEEN window logic or updateDevice writes would go undetected (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:51-70)

goldens.comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.

Authenticate hard-fails anonymous auth by returning ErrDeviceLimitReached as a raw untyped sentinel error instead of wrapping it in an authn-framework error (e.g., mapping to errUnauthenticated), so denied devices may surface as 500 Internal Server Error rather than a clean 401/denial

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go`, `Authenticate` now explicitly fails authentication by returning the raw `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached` (`return nil, err`) when `TagDevice` hits the device limit. The diff does not show any translation of this sentinel error into an authn/framework-specific unauthenticated/denied error type, so the concern that this may not be handled as a clean auth denial is grounded. However, the diff does not include the upstream error-to-HTTP-status mapping, so the claim that it will surface specifically as a 500 is not directly verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Existing devices inactive for >30 days (row present but outside the BETWEEN window, not yet cleaned up) get ErrDeviceLimitReached and are permanently denied — they can neither be updated nor re-created until cleanup frees a slot, causing hard lockout with no recovery path

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, when `deviceLimit > 0` and `count >= s.deviceLimit`, the code takes an update-only path (`return s.updateDevice(ctx, device)`) and never attempts the normal insert/upsert logic. But `updateDevice` updates only if the existing row’s `updated_at` is within the 30-day window (`WHERE device_id = ? AND updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?`). If a device row exists but is older than 30 days, the UPDATE affects 0 rows and `updateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. That means an existing (but stale) device cannot be refreshed/re-created while the limit is reached, until some cleanup deletes rows or the limit changes—matching the reported lockout scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MySQL no-op update can spuriously deny an existing active device: rowsAffected == 0 is treated exclusively as 'limit reached / device unknown', but on MySQL ROWS_AFFECTED counts changed rows (no CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS) at second-precision timestamps, so an identical update within the same second yields 0 affected rows and ErrDeviceLimitReached; SQLite-based tests won't catch this

adjudication.rationale: In `updateDevice` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go), the code treats `rowsAffected == 0` as `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. On MySQL/MariaDB, `RowsAffected` for an UPDATE can be 0 even when the row exists and the WHERE clause matched, if the new values are identical to existing values (default behavior without `CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS`). Since the UPDATE sets `client_ip`, `user_agent`, and especially `updated_at` from the passed-in `device` (which can be equal at DB precision, e.g., second precision), an existing active device can spuriously trigger `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when the device limit is reached. The added tests are DB-backed but don’t demonstrate MySQL semantics, so this defect is plausible and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 1-minute upper bound in updateDevice's updated_at BETWEEN window breaks under clock skew: comparing this instance's clock against updated_at written by another instance's clock means >1 minute skew (or NTP step-back) puts an active device outside the window, causing ErrDeviceLimitReached and denial of active devices

adjudication.rationale: In `updateDevice` the UPDATE only matches rows where `updated_at BETWEEN device.UpdatedAt-30d AND device.UpdatedAt+1m` (see args using `device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(time.Minute)`). Since `device.UpdatedAt` is set by the current process/request, in a multi-instance setup an existing row’s `updated_at` written by another instance with a clock >1 minute ahead (or if this instance’s clock steps back) can fall outside the `+1m` upper bound, causing `RowsAffected==0` and returning `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, effectively denying updates for an active device when the limit is reached.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tagging moved onto the synchronous request path with panic containment removed: goroutine, context.WithTimeout, and recover() were removed, so every anonymous request performs synchronous DB work (CountDevices plus a write) on the auth critical path, and panics in TagDevice propagate into the authn flow instead of being logged and contained

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows TagDevice was moved from an async goroutine with context.WithTimeout and a deferred recover() (now removed in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go) to a synchronous call on the Authenticate path: `if err := a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)`. This means tagging (which can hit the DB via anonstore.CreateOrUpdateDevice and, when `deviceLimit > 0`, can also call CountDevices) can now add latency/failure to the authn critical path, and any panic inside TagDevice would now propagate rather than being contained/logged. However, the finding overstates that *every* anonymous request will do `CountDevices + write`; TagDevice has local-cache behavior (see impl_test mention) and CountDevices only happens when `deviceLimit > 0` and limit logic is active.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change behavior so that `Authenticate` now calls `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` synchronously and explicitly returns the error when it is `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go). `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is a plain `fmt.Errorf("device limit reached")` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go), so this raw error is now propagated into the authn pipeline instead of being swallowed/logged as before. However, the claim that it will surface as a “500-style” status or show the raw text to unauthenticated users is not verifiable from this diff alone (depends on upstream error handling not shown). This is still a concrete, diff-grounded concern about error mapping/UX, not a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AnonymousDeviceLimit is exposed to all clients via the unauthenticated /frontend/settings payload, disclosing the configured anonymous capacity with no apparent consumer need (pkg/api/frontendsettings.go:198, pkg/api/dtos/frontend_settings.go:195)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `AnonymousDeviceLimit` being added to `FrontendSettingsDTO` and set in `getFrontendSettings`, and it’s also added to the frontend `GrafanaConfig`/`GrafanaBootConfig`, indicating an intended frontend consumer. However, the finding’s core claim hinges on assumptions not verifiable from the diff: that `/frontend/settings` is unauthenticated and that there is “no apparent consumer need.” The PR explicitly wires the value into the frontend config surface, contradicting the “no need” assertion, and the diff does not show endpoint auth behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Synchronous COUNT(*) added to authentication hot path: client.go removed fire-and-forget goroutine so TagDevice is now fully synchronous inside Authenticate, and every CreateOrUpdateDevice call with deviceLimit > 0 runs CountDevices (a COUNT(*) query) before any insert/update, causing a potential table scan on anon_device per invocation and a latency/DB-load amplifier under high device churn

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifies the described performance concern: `Anonymous.Authenticate` in `client.go` no longer spawns a fire-and-forget goroutine with its own timeout; it now calls `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` synchronously in the authentication path. In `anonstore/database.go`, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` adds a `deviceLimit > 0` branch that calls `s.CountDevices(...)` (a COUNT query) on every invocation until the limit is reached, before doing the insert/upsert. This is a concrete, diff-grounded latency/DB-load regression risk rather than a direct correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Count-then-insert TOCTOU race: the count check and insert in CreateOrUpdateDevice are not atomic, so under concurrent requests N simultaneous new devices can all observe count < limit and all insert, overshooting the device limit; the ErrDeviceLimitReached compensation in updateDevice only kicks in for the next request

adjudication.rationale: In `AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`, the new device-limit enforcement does a separate `CountDevices(...)` check and then (if under limit) proceeds to insert/upsert a device. This check is not performed in the same DB transaction/locking context as the subsequent insert, so concurrent requests can all observe `count < s.deviceLimit` and each insert a new device, temporarily (or permanently) exceeding the configured limit. The fallback `updateDevice`/`ErrDeviceLimitReached` path only triggers when `count >= limit`, so it doesn’t prevent overshoot in that race window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Once the device limit is reached, every returning (cached-out) device still pays the expensive COUNT query before its cheap UPDATE, doubling work on the steady-state path; a conditional UPDATE first with COUNT only when rowsAffected == 0 would be cheaper

adjudication.rationale: In `AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`, when `s.deviceLimit > 0` it always executes `s.CountDevices(...)` first, and only then may call `s.updateDevice(...)` if `count >= s.deviceLimit` (or proceed to insert/upsert otherwise). This means once the system is at/near the limit, every subsequent request pays the extra COUNT query even if the device already exists and could be handled by a cheap UPDATE first. The suggested approach (try UPDATE, and only COUNT when no rows were affected) is a concrete, diff-grounded performance improvement rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ListDevices API returns unbounded result set with no pagination or LIMIT, materializing all devices in the 30-day window into a single JSON response, which can spike memory and response time on the Grafana server

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/api/api.go`, `ListDevices` always queries a full 30-day window (`fromTime := time.Now().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration)`) and calls `api.store.ListDevices(...)` with no limit/pagination parameters. The store interface `ListDevices(ctx, from, to) ([]*Device, error)` also has no way to request a bounded page, implying the API response size grows with the number of devices in that window. While not necessarily a correctness bug introduced by this diff, it is a concrete performance/scalability concern observable from the diff (unpaginated endpoint returning a slice).

adjudication_records.issue_text: ErrDeviceLimitReached propagates out of Authenticate as an authentication failure, so once the device limit is hit new anonymous users get hard auth errors; combined with the TOCTOU race an attacker can race-fill the limit and lock out all subsequent new anonymous visitors (denial-of-service-by-design)

adjudication.rationale: In `updateDevice` the code treats `RowsAffected()==0` as meaning “no eligible device existed” and returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. However it issues an `UPDATE anon_device SET client_ip=?, user_agent=?, updated_at=? ...` and relies solely on `sql.Result.RowsAffected()`. For MySQL, `RowsAffected` can be 0 even when a row matches the `WHERE` clause but the new values are identical to the existing values (default “changed rows” semantics), so an already-known device could spuriously trigger `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when the limit is reached. This behavior is grounded in the diff: `rowsAffected==0` directly maps to `ErrDeviceLimitReached` in `updateDevice`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Undefined HTTP contract when device limit is hit (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-53): Authenticate now returns raw anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached which is not a recognized authn error type, leaving the HTTP response (401 vs 500, redirect vs JSON, message exposure) undefined; needs deliberate error mapping or should proceed unauthenticated instead of failing auth

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a behavior change in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go`: `Authenticate` now calls `TagDevice` synchronously and, on `errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached)`, returns `nil, err` where `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is a plain `fmt.Errorf` from the store. There is no mapping in this diff to an `authn`-specific/typed error or to a deliberate HTTP status/response shape, so how this propagates to HTTP (401/403/429/500, redirects vs JSON, message exposure) depends on code not shown. The concern about needing deliberate error mapping is grounded, but the exact “undefined HTTP contract” outcome cannot be fully verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Synchronous DB write plus CountDevices query added to the anonymous request hot path (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-53): the goroutine + context.WithTimeout + panic recovery was removed, causing latency/DB-load regression on every anonymous request

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the anonymous auth flow changed from async tagging to synchronous tagging: in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go` the goroutine, `context.WithTimeout(...)`, and panic recovery wrapper were removed and replaced with a direct call `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` that can now block the request path. Additionally, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go` now performs a `CountDevices(...)` query (and potentially an `UPDATE`/`INSERT`) when `deviceLimit > 0`, which is work that can occur during `TagDevice`. This is a diff-grounded performance/latency regression concern, though not a direct correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: TagDevice now runs with the request context instead of a detached context (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-53), so client-disconnected/aborted requests silently lose device tagging that was previously guaranteed to complete in the background

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows Authenticate() in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go changed from spawning a goroutine using context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Minute) to calling a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...) inline with the request context. That means if the request context is canceled (e.g., client disconnect/abort), TagDevice can be canceled and the device may not get tagged, whereas previously tagging would continue independently for up to the timeout. This is a concrete behavior change, but the diff doesn’t prove it’s an outright defect (it may be intentional to avoid background work), so it’s best treated as a non-bug review concern about changed reliability/semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: A panic in TagDevice is no longer recovered and logged (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-53) and can now propagate into the authn flow and surface as a 500

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the goroutine wrapper with a `defer`/`recover()` around the TagDevice call in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go` (previously lines ~44-53). It is now called synchronously without any local panic recovery, so any panic inside `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(...)` would indeed propagate up the authn `Authenticate` call stack (whereas before it would be recovered and only logged in the goroutine). Whether this results in a 500 depends on higher-level recovery middleware not shown in the diff, so the impact is a robustness/regression concern rather than a directly provable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Response-shape drift (pkg/api/dtos/frontend_settings.go:195, packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200, packages/grafana-runtime/src/config.ts:97): AnonymousDeviceLimit is int64 without omitempty so the server always sends a number, but the TS type declares number | undefined; undefined can never arrive, making '!== undefined' checks dead code, and the 0-vs-undefined semantics are undocumented; pick one sentinel

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows backend always includes `anonymousDeviceLimit` as an `int64` in `FrontendSettingsDTO` with no `omitempty` (so JSON will always have a number, defaulting to 0 via `MustInt64(0)` in `readAuthSettings`). Meanwhile TS declares `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined` and runtime boot config sets it to `undefined`, creating a real API/typing mismatch and unclear 0-vs-undefined semantics, though not necessarily a concrete runtime failure in this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: TOCTOU race in CreateOrUpdateDevice (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:94-102): count-then-act with no transaction, lock, or conditional insert lets concurrent first-arrivals exceed the configured device limit; consider a conditional insert mechanism like the updateDevice guard

adjudication.rationale: The new device-limit enforcement in `CreateOrUpdateDevice` does a separate `CountDevices(...)` call and, if below the limit, proceeds to insert/update without any transaction, lock, or conditional insert. Under concurrent requests, multiple goroutines can observe `count < deviceLimit` and all insert, allowing the number of stored devices to exceed `s.deviceLimit`. The diff shows no DB-level constraint or atomic guard to prevent this (the `updateDevice` guard only runs when `count >= deviceLimit`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Wire constructor signature changes (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:37-46, anonstore/database.go:57-59): ProvideAnonymousDeviceService drops the anonStore parameter and ProvideAnonDBStore gains one, but no wire_gen.go update appears in the diff; a stale wire set would cause a build/initialization failure

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes provider signatures: ProvideAnonDBStore now requires a deviceLimit parameter (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go), and ProvideAnonymousDeviceService drops the anonStore parameter and instead constructs the store from sqlStore+cfg (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go). However, the diff alone cannot confirm whether Wire is used for these providers or whether wire_gen.go is updated elsewhere in the PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Synchronous DB call in anonymous auth hot path with no timeout — removal of detached goroutine with context.WithTimeout means slow/hanging DB blocks every anonymous request (client.go:44-49)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the detached goroutine + explicit timeout: client.go previously did `go ... context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), timeoutTag)` around `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(...)`, but now calls `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, httpReqCopy, ...)` synchronously. From the diff, `TagDevice` can hit the DB via `anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` (see anonstore/database.go and impl.go wiring), and no new timeout is introduced. This can increase tail latency / risk blocking the anonymous auth request if the DB is slow, but it’s not a strictly verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone (it may be intentional to enforce `ErrDeviceLimitReached`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Lost crash isolation — old goroutine had recover(), now a panic in TagDevice propagates into auth path and fails the request instead of just logging a warning (client.go:44-49)

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the fire-and-forget goroutine wrapper (with a deferred recover) around `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(...)` in `client.go` and instead calls it inline, returning an error for `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and logging others. This does reduce crash isolation: if `TagDevice` (or code it calls) panics, it would now panic on the auth request path rather than being contained in a goroutine with `recover()`. However, the diff does not show any actual panic being introduced or that `TagDevice` is expected to panic, so this is a robustness/architecture concern rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Race condition in CreateOrUpdateDevice — CountDevices and INSERT are non-transactional, concurrent requests can all observe count < limit and insert, unboundedly exceeding the device limit (database.go:106-114)

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (database.go), the device-limit enforcement is implemented as a separate `CountDevices(...)` call followed by a subsequent insert/upsert path when `count < s.deviceLimit`. These operations are not wrapped in a single transaction or protected by a DB-side constraint/lock in the diff, so concurrent requests can all observe `count < limit` and proceed to insert, exceeding `deviceLimit`. This is a real correctness bug in the newly added limit logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: RowsAffected == 0 conflates 'device missing' with 'no rows changed' in MySQL — DSN without clientFoundRows=true returns rows changed, so an existing device with identical values gets spurious ErrDeviceLimitReached (database.go:72-92)

adjudication.rationale: In `updateDevice` (database.go), the code treats `rowsAffected == 0` as `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. But for MySQL, `RowsAffected()` commonly reports “rows changed”, not “rows matched”, unless the DSN enables `clientFoundRows=true`. If an existing `anon_device` row matches the `WHERE` but the `SET` values are identical (including `updated_at` if the caller reuses the same timestamp), MySQL can return 0 affected rows, causing a spurious `ErrDeviceLimitReached` even though the device exists and the update was logically allowed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Clock-skew window in updateDevice — hardcoded +1 minute tolerance in BETWEEN guard means devices with updated_at slightly in the future are locked out until the deletion job removes them, up to 30+ days (database.go:71-83)

adjudication.rationale: `updateDevice` uses `updated_at BETWEEN (device.UpdatedAt-30d) AND (device.UpdatedAt+1m)` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go). When the device limit is reached, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` calls `updateDevice`; if the existing DB row’s `updated_at` is >1 minute in the future relative to the incoming `device.UpdatedAt`, the UPDATE matches 0 rows and returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, which then bubbles up to anonymous authentication and can block access. The finding’s mention of waiting for a deletion job/30+ days is not strictly accurate (it would unblock once time catches up), but the hard +1 minute skew window can indeed cause erroneous lockouts under clock-skew/future timestamps.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: ErrDeviceLimitReached sentinel error surfaced through Authenticate with no HTTP status mapping or user-facing message, producing opaque hard failure for anonymous visitors (client.go:46-48)

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes device tagging synchronous in `Anonymous.Authenticate` and explicitly returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` up the auth stack (`client.go`), whereas previously failures were only logged in a goroutine. The finding’s core concern—this sentinel error now bubbles out with no local translation to a specific HTTP response/message—is grounded in the diff (no mapping/wrapping is added here). Whether this is a “bug” depends on intended UX (blocking anonymous auth when limit reached may be desired), but it is a concrete, change-introduced behavior/handling concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Additional DB round-trip per anonymous request — CountDevices aggregate plus conditional write on every cache-miss tagging creates hot-path cost and load amplifier during traffic spikes (database.go:106-113)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `deviceLimit` feature where `CreateOrUpdateDevice` performs a `CountDevices(...)` query when `s.deviceLimit > 0` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go, in the new block before the insert/upsert). If the limit is reached it then issues an `UPDATE` via `updateDevice`; otherwise it proceeds to the usual insert/upsert. This introduces at least one extra DB query (the COUNT) on each tagging call that reaches the store (e.g., cache-miss in the service), which is a real, diff-grounded hot-path performance concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Frontend config type declares AnonymousDeviceLimit as number | undefined but backend DTO always serializes a number (0 when unset), causing inconsistent behavior for logic branching on === undefined (config.ts:200 / frontend_settings.go:195)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a real contract/type mismatch: the frontend `GrafanaConfig` declares `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined` and `GrafanaBootConfig` initializes it to `undefined`, but the backend `FrontendSettingsDTO` defines `AnonymousDeviceLimit int64` and always assigns `hs.Cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit`, which is read via `MustInt64(0)` (so it will be `0` when unset). Thus the backend will serialize a number (including 0) rather than `undefined`/omitting the field. However, the claim about breaking frontend logic branching on `=== undefined` is not directly verifiable from this diff since no such frontend logic is shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Missing test coverage for updateDevice success path — no test calls updateDevice with an existing device_id within the 30-day window and asserts no error and that client_ip, user_agent, and updated_at are persisted

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial logic in `AnonDBStore.updateDevice` (UPDATE with an `updated_at BETWEEN ...` window and returning `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when `RowsAffected()==0`). Existing tests only cover the failure path when the device limit is hit and the device does not already exist (`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` sets `deviceLimit=1`, inserts one device, then tries a different `DeviceID`, expecting `ErrDeviceLimitReached`). There is no test that hits the success path: reaching the limit and then calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice` with an already-existing `device_id` within the 30-day window and asserting it returns nil and that `client_ip`, `user_agent`, and `updated_at` are actually updated in the DB.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Significant behavioral change to Authenticate with no corresponding test — TagDevice is now synchronous (blocking auth on DB latency) and ErrDeviceLimitReached now fails authentication entirely, with no test verifying anonymous auth errors on limit hit or succeeds on non-limit TagDevice failure
matched_golden_ids: Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same behavioral regression: TagDevice is now synchronous and ErrDeviceLimitReached causes Authenticate to fail, preventing anonymous authentication when the device limit is reached (previously non-blocking/asynchronous). Extra mention of missing tests doesn’t change the core match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks the error and never asserts database state via ListDevices to confirm the rejected device was not inserted and exactly one device row remains

adjudication.rationale: In `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit`, the test sets `ProvideAnonDBStore(store, 1)`, inserts one device successfully, then attempts a second insert and only asserts `require.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrDeviceLimitReached)`. It never calls `ListDevices`/`CountDevices` afterward to verify the DB state (e.g., that the second device was not inserted and that only one row remains). This is a specific, diff-grounded gap in testing the new device-limit behavior, not a verifiable functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Boundary condition of the device limit (count == limit-1 → create succeeds; count == limit → rejected) is only half-covered (limit=1 only)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an integration test `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` that, with `deviceLimit=1`, exercises both boundary behaviors: when `count == limit-1` (0 < 1) the first `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds, and when `count == limit` (1 >= 1) the second call is rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. So it is not “only half-covered” for the stated boundary condition; it is covered for the boundary at limit=1.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: No edge-case coverage for expired devices interacting with the limit — a device with updated_at older than 30 days is excluded from the count but also from the updateDevice BETWEEN window, so it can never refresh itself and always receives ErrDeviceLimitReached; behavior of stale/expired devices under a configured limit is unpinned

adjudication.rationale: The new limit logic in `CreateOrUpdateDevice` counts only devices updated within the last 30 days (`CountDevices(... now-30d, now+1m)`) and, when the limit is reached, calls `updateDevice`. But `updateDevice` only updates rows whose *existing* `updated_at` falls within a 30-day window relative to the incoming `device.UpdatedAt` (`WHERE device_id = ? AND updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?`). If a device record is older than the expiration window and the limit is reached, the update will affect 0 rows and return `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. There is no test covering this expired-device interaction (tests only use `UpdatedAt: time.Now().Add(-time.Hour)`), so the intended behavior for stale/expired devices under limit isn’t pinned by coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Config propagation to frontend is untested — AnonymousDeviceLimit int64 serializes as 0 when unset, but the TS type is number | undefined and runtime default is undefined, so consumers may interpret 0 as 'limit of zero devices'; no test asserts the serialized payload for configured and unconfigured cases

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows a mismatch in how `AnonymousDeviceLimit` is represented across layers without any test coverage of the serialized frontend payload: backend config `Cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit int64` is always set (defaults via `MustInt64(0)` in `readAuthSettings`) and `FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit int64` (no `omitempty`) will always serialize as `0` when unset (`getFrontendSettings` assigns `hs.Cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit`). Meanwhile the TS config surface adds `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined` and `GrafanaBootConfig` defaults it to `undefined`. The finding’s core point (propagation/serialization behavior is untested and the representations differ) is grounded in the diff, though whether consumers will misinterpret `0` as “zero devices” isn’t verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: No coverage for the TagDevice contract change in impl.go — tagDeviceUI errors were previously swallowed (logged, returned nil) and are now propagated, but no test exercises the failure path

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go`, `TagDevice` now returns the error from `a.tagDeviceUI(...)` (added `return err` inside the `if err != nil` block). Previously this path only logged (`a.log.Debug(...)`) and then fell through to `return nil`, so the observable contract changed from “swallow tagDeviceUI errors” to “propagate tagDeviceUI errors”. The integration tests in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl_test.go` only assert successful tagging (`require.NoError`) and do not exercise a failing `tagDeviceUI`/store path to verify the new behavior (or its impact on callers).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Check-then-act race on the device limit (CountDevices + conditional insert) is untested — concurrent anonymous requests can overshoot the limit, and no concurrency test documents whether slight overshoot is acceptable

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice` the new limit enforcement does a non-atomic check-then-act: it calls `CountDevices(...)` and, if `count < s.deviceLimit`, proceeds to the normal insert/upsert path; otherwise it calls `s.updateDevice(...)` (which can return `ErrDeviceLimitReached`). Under concurrent requests, multiple goroutines can observe `count < limit` and both insert, temporarily overshooting the limit. The added test `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only covers a sequential case (limit=1 then insert a second device) and does not document/verify concurrent behavior or whether overshoot is acceptable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Device limit is trivially exhaustible — anonymous device identity is client-supplied, so an attacker can fill the device table with fresh device IDs up to the limit, causing a hard authentication failure (error page, not login redirect) for all new anonymous devices; entries persist 30 days and recovery requires admin intervention; the exact limit is exposed to unauthenticated clients via FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit, and there is no rate limiting on the first-seen/create path (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-48, pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:97-103)

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes anonymous authentication fail hard when the device limit is reached: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` once `CountDevices(...) >= s.deviceLimit` and the device ID cannot be updated (`updateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` on `rowsAffected == 0`) (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go). That error is now propagated up (`TagDevice` returns the error; pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go) and `Authenticate` returns the error for `ErrDeviceLimitReached` instead of continuing (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go), so new anonymous sessions/devices are denied once the table hits the limit (devices are counted over the last 30 days via `anonymousDeviceExpiration`). The limit is also exposed to clients via `FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit` (pkg/api/dtos/frontend_settings.go, pkg/api/frontendsettings.go), making the threshold discoverable. Whether the device ID is strictly “client-supplied” isn’t proven in this diff, but the introduced behavior is still exhaustible by repeatedly creating new devices and results in a denial of anonymous access.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: TOCTOU race in CreateOrUpdateDevice — CountDevices then insert is not atomic (no transaction, row lock, or INSERT ... WHERE count < limit guard), so N concurrent requests from new devices can all observe count < limit and all insert, exceeding the limit (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:95-103)
matched_golden_ids: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes a TOCTOU race where CountDevices and insert are not atomic, allowing concurrent requests to all pass the count check and exceed the device limit, and it suggests using transactions/locks/guards. This is the same underlying race condition as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: updateDevice conflates rowsAffected == 0 with 'device limit reached' — zero affected rows can have unrelated causes (MySQL changed-rows semantics without CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS when values are identical due to DATETIME second precision, or clock skew in HA deployments where a future updated_at from a node running ahead causes the BETWEEN match to fail), spuriously blocking legitimate known devices with a device-limit error (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:72-93)

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go, updateDevice() maps `rowsAffected == 0` to `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. But the UPDATE can legitimately affect 0 rows for reasons unrelated to “device limit reached”: (1) the row matches but no column actually changes (common MySQL semantics without CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS), e.g. repeated calls within the same stored timestamp precision where `updated_at` resolves to the same value and `client_ip`/`user_agent` are unchanged; (2) the `updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?` predicate can fail due to time skew/future timestamps, even for an existing device. In both cases the code returns a misleading device-limit error and can block known devices once the limit is hit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Tagging moved onto the synchronous request path with panic recovery removed — previously fire-and-forget goroutine with recover() and detached 2-minute timeout, now any panic in the tagging chain propagates into authentication and fails the request, and every anonymous request's latency now includes the store round-trip so DB slowness stalls all anonymous traffic (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-50)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Authenticate` in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go` no longer spawns a fire-and-forget goroutine with `recover()` and a detached 2-minute timeout; it now calls `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` synchronously on the request path and only special-cases `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached` to fail auth. This means anonymous request latency can now include the tagging/store work and a slow DB can block authentication. However, the claim that “any panic propagates and fails the request” is only partially verifiable: the local `recover()` was removed, but whether a panic would actually fail the request (vs being recovered by higher-level middleware) is not shown in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Device limit silently fails open on any DB error — if CountDevices or the store call returns any error other than ErrDeviceLimitReached, the device is not registered and the error is only warn-logged, so during DB degradation the limit is silently unenforced with no operator signal (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:97-101, pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:50-52)

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows anonymous authentication only hard-fails on `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached` (client.go: if `TagDevice` returns other errors, it logs a warn and still returns an anonymous identity). In the store, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns DB errors from `CountDevices` / insert/update paths directly (database.go), which will be ignored by the auth path except for warn logging. This means the device-limit mechanism won’t be enforced under DB errors, but that appears to be an intentional availability tradeoff rather than a clearly verifiable defect; also it’s not fully “silent” because it warn-logs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Test gap — TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only asserts a new device gets ErrDeviceLimitReached; it never verifies that an existing in-window device still succeeds via updateDevice when count >= limit, nor that the device count didn't grow, so regressions in the BETWEEN window logic or updateDevice writes would go undetected (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:51-70)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial device-limit logic in AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(): when CountDevices() >= deviceLimit it calls updateDevice(), which uses an UPDATE ... WHERE device_id = ? AND updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ? and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0. The new TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit (database_test.go) only covers the “new device rejected” path by changing DeviceID to a new value and expecting ErrDeviceLimitReached; it does not cover the intended “existing device within window updates successfully” path nor assert that device count remains unchanged when the limit is hit. That leaves regressions in the BETWEEN window/update write behavior untested.
